title: Francisco Murguía to Pablo González, Lamadrid, 16 March 1914 (catalogue 1465): Clave Extra 3 with a contemporary pencil decipherment on the typed copy; key rebuilt from it, frozen and tested on held-out page 4 (0.842 letter agreement), letter read from the figures

steps.what: LXVIII-1.2.56.1, 2.75.1, 7.890.1, 14.1943.1 (4 pages), 17.2435.1, 23.3148.1 and 23.3165.1 fetched from the CEHM image server one at a time, 2 s apart; 8.957.1-2 returned 404.

Sign conventions written first. The 488 groups transcribed twice, from the original (pp. 1-2) and from fresh crops of the copy (pp. 3-4) with the pencil layer covered: same group at 487 of 488 places (S11 g22 over-struck in both).

scripts/build_key.py aligns the figures with the pencil letters by dynamic programming and takes the majority value per group: 45 cells. 5 cells set by hand where the aligner split word groups wrongly (46, 49, 87, 91, 99); 10 unattested cells filled from the table layout; 88 and 97 left open. key.tsv 62 entries, key_frozen.tsv 60, frozen 12 Nov 2026.

Held-out: key built from page-3 segments S01-S15 only, frozen, applied to page-4 segments S16-S23 (217 groups): letter agreement with the pencil gloss 0.842 over 240 letters; 200 keys with shuffled values at most 0.154. Errors from 8 groups absent from page 3 and two word groups the aligner split wrongly (scripts/heldout.py, work/heldout_out.txt).

Decrypted mechanically with key_frozen.tsv and read as sentences with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py rebuilds each run and passes (23 runs, 4 marks, 0 failures). 103 coded words: 99 verbatim, 2 with an added letter, 2 guessed (97, 88). Five places where the figures differ from the pencil gloss are listed.

Web searches (Pablo González 1913-1914 clave; cifrados constitucionalistas; Narváez, 'Algunos casos criptográficos del movimiento constitucionalista, 1914-1915', Historia Mexicana 75/2, 2025), repeated once by the reviewer on 13 Nov: no edition or decipherment of these documents or of Clave Extra 3. Narváez 2025 (403 to a script) and 2019, and M. W. González, Con Carranza (1933-34), not read.

Independent blind review by a second AI language-model agent (13 Nov 2026): 59 of 59 groups of p. 4 agree on its own crops; check_marks.py, decrypt.py and heldout.py reproduced; build_key.py confirmed to read only training segments in the held-out run; reading graded A.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 486 tokens, 50 types, es-modern order 4: reading -2.104 per letter; random keys -6.186 (z 9.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.469 (mean -3.566, z 17.5); annealer on the real text -2.307. Verdict: pass.

Integration check by the repository: heldout.py (0.842 on page 4, shuffled max 0.154) and check_marks.py reproduced; own decoder from key_frozen.tsv gives the same 23 decryptions; all 217 groups of S16-S23 compared with the CEHM image .0004 (typed copy, pencil layer visible): all agree. Own statistical check (es-modern): -2.104 per letter against -6.186 for random keys (z 9.3), pass. Strict word share 99 of 104 = 95.2% (the supplied [por] counts as a hole); class read, key partial.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) reading only key.tsv, run on the 23 segments of transcription_LXVIII-1.14.1943.1.txt: 488 groups, the decoded segments identical to decryption_LXVIII-1.14.1943.1.txt in all 23. Key layout checked: each decade is a reversed alphabet block (10-19 and 20-29 a j i h g f e d c b; 30-39 and 40-49 l rr r q p o ñ n m ll; 50-59 and 60-69 s . . z y x w v u t), and every value from the pairs fits it. CEHM scan p. 1 re-read: groups 88 and 97 are clearly typed, and the S11 over-strike is 58 or 68 (both u). Reading note: S13 decodes 'tomarla' (69 35 38 10 42 40 10); with 88 = 'por' the sentence needs no supplied [por] ('no habiéndonos sido posible tomarla por ser el enemigo ...'), but 78 is already por and 88 occurs once, so this stays a guess. Read bar: the recorded 0.952 (99 of 104 words) follows the README; research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.measure returns 0.985 because v2_score.holes does not count the {+x} restorations.

Project check of PR #565 (Brice Dudout): his independent decoder re-run (23 segments, 488 groups, identical to the published decryption). CEHM scan p. 1 (LXVIII-1.14.1943.1.0001) compared with S10-S15: 120 groups, all as transcribed; 88 (S13) and 97 (S12) clearly typed; S11 over-strike 58/68 seen. His suggestion 88 = por is recorded as a possibility only and not counted (78 is already por; 88 occurs once). The recorded 0.952 (99 of 104 coded words) stands; v10_relabel.measure gives 0.985 because v2_score.holes ignores {+x} markers (tooling note).

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.104; polyphony 0.0; 2 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.307

outcome.method_basis: The typed copy (pp. 3-4) carries a contemporary pencil decipherment of every coded run but two groups. The key was rebuilt from figures and pencil, frozen, tested on held-out page 4, and the reading was made from the figures with that key, with the departures from the pencil gloss listed.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Strict README rule on the coded runs (scripts/count_words.py counts plus the supplied word): 99 of 104 words read as typed (95.2%); 2 with a marked added letter (NACI{+O}NAL, MOLIN{+O}), 2 guessed (groups 97 and 88) and the supplied '[por]' are not counted as read. The contributor's figure is 99 of 103 (96.1%), which leaves '[por]' out. The clear text (most of the letter) reads in full.

texts.label: Murguía to González, Lamadrid, 16 Mar 1914
texts.summary: Murguía reports his campaign of 4-15 March 1914: the Nacional railway cut between Golondrinas and Huisachito, Monclova taken with Castro on the 10th and lost on the 11th to more than a thousand men from Monterrey, a fall-back to San Buenaventura and the Molino del Águila, a failed attack on the 15th and a retreat to Lamadrid; his ammunition is spent and he is sending a commission to Ciudad Juárez by way of Sierra Mojada for 200,000 cartridges.
texts.note: 103 coded words in 23 runs: 99 verbatim from the signs (96.1%, the contributor's figure; 99 of 104 = 95.2% when the supplied [por] counts, the share used here), 2 with a marked added letter, 2 guessed ([?no:97], [?plaza:88]); '[por]' supplied and not counted. The contemporary pencil decipherment on pp. 3-4 gives the same text, with five differences listed in the reading.

reading_review.note: Reads as continuous sentences and the translation follows; the holes [?no:97], [?plaza:88] and the supplied [por] are marked, and the differences between figures and pencil gloss are listed. It is an existing contemporary decipherment and is credited as such.

gaps.detail: One occurrence each, not glossed; the sense suggests 'plaza' (or 'plaza por') and 'no'.
Over-struck in both exemplars (58 or 68); both are u, so the reading does not depend on it.

prior.where: Contemporary pencil interlinear decipherment on the typed copy, pp. 3-4 of LXVIII-1.14.1943.1 itself. No edition or decipherment in print found (web searches 12-13 Nov 2026; Narváez 2019 and 2025 and M. W. González, Con Carranza, not read).

human: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1465) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed the figures twice, built or fitted and froze the key, decrypted, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
